question: **Select the sentence with the appropriate use of preposition.**
solution:
The correct answer is** 'He arrived on Sunday morning.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct sentence with the appropriate use of preposition is **option 4) "He arrived on Sunday morning."**
 
• When referring to a specific point in time, such as a particular day or time of day, we use the preposition **"on." **
 
• In this case, **"Sunday morning"** is a specific time when the person arrived, so the correct preposition to use is** "on."**
 
 
• Example: "He arrived** on** Monday evening."
 
 
 
• Therefore,** option 4) "He arrived on Sunday morning"** is the correct answer as it follows the grammatical rule of using the preposition "on" when referring to a specific day or time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other options:
 
• **"He arrived to Sunday morning" **uses the incorrect preposition "to." We do not use "to" when referring to a specific day or time.
 
• **"He arrived at Sunday morning"** uses the incorrect preposition "at." While "at" can be used to indicate a general time or place, it is not the appropriate preposition to indicate a specific point in time like "Sunday morning."
 
• **"He arrived in Sunday morning" **uses the incorrect preposition "in." We use "in" to indicate a general time period or season, but not for a specific point in time like "Sunday morning."
